To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the burning rate is a non-monotonic function of curvature and it has two extrema: one minimum and one maximum.
the Michelson–Markstein burning rate effect is confirmed experimentally for a solid homogeneous energetic propellant.

the burning rate of solid homogeneous energetic material depends on the curvature of the burning front and the dependence of the burning front curvature on the burning rate is described by the Zel'dovič-Novozhilov's formula.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the influence of the curvature of the surface of a solid homogeneous explosive on its burning rate.
the Michelson–Markstein's effect for solid homogeneous energetic materials.
the development of a new method for experimental determination of the dependence of the burning velocity on the curvature.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the burning rate of solid homogeneous energetic material is not dependent on curvature of the surface.
the Michelson–Markstein's effect in combustion of a solid homogeneous propellant is not observed.
the Michelson–Markstein coefficient in the case of the combustion of solid homogeneous materials is negative.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the burning rate of solid homogeneous energetic material is not a function of the burning surface curvature.
the burning rates for the propellant grains with the curved surfaces are in good agreement with the theoretical predictions of the Zel’dovich–Novozilov’s model.
we have experimentally confirmed the existence of the dependence of the burning surface curvature on the burning rate for solid homogeneous energetic materials.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Michelson–Markstein coefficient for a homogeneous energetic material is negative.
the dependence of the burning rates of energetic materials on the surface curvature is not negligible.
the Michelson–Markstein coefficient for the double slit is positive and its absolute value is about 2–4 times larger than the coefficient obtained for a single slit of the same width.
